newsitem.title: UK: Iraq snubs BP, Shell requests for crude contracts.
newsitem.headline: Iraq snubs BP, Shell requests for crude contracts.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch Shell and British Petroleum plc said on Thursday Iraq had decided against renewing oil sale contracts to the companies under the United Nation's humanitarian oil-for-food exchange.
"We had asked to renew our existing contract. We have been official advised by SOMO that we would not receive an allocation," said a BP spokesman.
SOMO is Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation responsible for selling crude under arrangements with the United Nations.
"Our contract has not been renewed and we are awaiting the outcome of enquiries to clarify the matter," said a Shell spokesman.
Iraq's second phase of oil sales under the U.N. arrangements are expected to start in a few days following a two-month delay to allow modifications to aid distribution plans.
In the first six-month oil sale which started last December BP secured a 10,000 barrel a day (bpd) contract for Iraq's Kirkuk crude and Shell took 30,000 bpd.
The oil-for-food programme was set up to alleviate the impact on civilians of sanctions imposed on Iraq after its troops invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Rasheed said in Baghdad on Wednesday that companies from countries deemed friendly to Iraq would get preferential treatment on oil sale contracts.
Japanese oil refiners on Thursday said they were concerned that Iraq would decide not to renew contracts because of political differences with Tokyo.
"We have been notified by our head office that Baghdad has decided not to allocate to Japan in August," said a Singapore trader with a Japanese refiner that was also pursuing Iraqi barrels.
Japan companies as a whole are hoping to secure at least 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi exports.
Both Mitsubishi Corp, which is representing four Japan refiners, and Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd have sent negotiators to Baghdad for contract talks.
